channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Further weakness could target 157.30 against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/JPY surged above 156.30 to a high of 156.41, with momentum still modest but supportive of further gains. Intraday, the pair could test 156.50 while holding above support at 155.40.

item.title: Euro: Stabilizing with policy support – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret say EUR/USD is stabilizing after Wednesday’s Fed decision, as improving Germany-US 2-year yield spreads and a hawkish ECB stance support the euro.

item.title: Australian Dollar rebound offsets the hawkish Fed hike
item.description: AUD/USD rebounds near the 0.7110s area on Thursday after the pair spent recent sessions nursing losses on bets for a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed). At the time of writing, the pair rises by over 0.40%, but the rebound has little to do with anything out of Australia.

item.title: 1.25%: Why the Bank of Japan hike is a done deal and the Japanese Yen now hinges on Ueda's guidance
item.description: The Bank of Japan (BoJ) stands on the verge of delivering a 25 basis point rate hike to 1.25%, with financial markets pricing in a near 100% probability of such an action.

item.title: Bank of England: Cautious hold with upside risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ macro team, led by Pooja Kumra, notes the Bank of England kept Bank Rate at 3.75% in a 6-3 vote, with a more hawkish tone versus July as inflation risks stay skewed higher.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed hike keeps upside risks – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the US Dollar (USD) is holding gains after a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) hike, with 10-year Treasury yields retreating and equities firmer. The FOMC raised rates by 25bps and signaled more work is needed to bring inflation back to target.

item.title: Gold climbs over 2% as US Dollar trims post-Fed gains
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rebounds on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) trims some of the gains driven by the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) hawkish monetary policy announcement. A cooldown in the Oil rally also pulls US Treasury yields away from their recent highs, lending additional support to the precious metal.

item.title: Euro gains against US Dollar as post-Fed rally loses momentum
item.description: EUR/USD trades modestly higher on Thursday as falling Oil prices pull US Treasury yields away from their recent highs, prompting the US Dollar (USD) to trim part of its post-Fed gains.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Two more hikes seen as inflation stays too high – UOB
item.description: UOB’s economics team, led by Suan Teck Kin and Alvin Liew, interprets the September FOMC as the start of a short hiking extension rather than a one-off move.

item.title: British Pound: Bearish against Euro after BoE hold – TD Securities
item.description: FX strategist Howard Du at TD Securities reiterates a bullish EUR/GBP stance after the Bank of England’s (BoE) cautious hold.

item.title: Canadian Dollar remains under pressure as USD/CAD flirts with 1.4000
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3980 on Thursday at the time of writing, little changed on the day and hovering near the psychological 1.4000 level. The US Dollar (USD) remains supported by better-than-expected employment data, while the Canadian Dollar (CAD) continues to face pressure from weak Oil prices.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ tightening expectations lift JPY against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight USD/JPY trading near 155.65 with the Japanese Yen (JPY) outperforming G10 peers as markets price in a Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike alongside elevated domestic risk around CPI and policy decisions.

item.title: Bank of England: November hike risk rises – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Stefan Koopman notes that the Bank of England kept Bank Rate at 3.75% in a 6-3 vote, but sees rising inflation risks from higher energy prices and the Middle East conflict.

item.title: Euro: Downside levels in focus against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang highlights building downside momentum in EUR/USD as the 21‑day EMA approaches a bearish cross below the 55‑day EMA. The pair has broken below the Ichimoku cloud and key moving averages, with support at 1.1400 and subsequent levels at 1.1353 and 1.1324.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Underperformance persists on wider spreads – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight that USD/CAD remains elevated near 1.40 after the FOMC, with the Canadian Dollar (CAD) underperforming peers as the Fed/BoC rate differential returns to 175bps.

item.title: WTI Oil Price Forecast: Bulls lose momentum near $100
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil extends its decline on Thursday, sliding nearly 2% as Saudi Arabia’s rerouting efforts and hopes for a faster pipeline recovery weigh on prices, even as broader Middle East supply risks stay elevated.

item.title: British Pound: BoE stance leaves Pound exposed – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that the Bank of England (BoE) kept Bank Rate at 3.75% but signaled a low bar for further tightening. Governor Bailey warned policy may have to tighten if Middle East conflict-driven second-round effects emerge.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Faster BoJ tightening supports gains against US Dollar - MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Halpenny expects the BoJ to deliver a 25bps hike to 1.25%, with communications outlining further rate increases and supporting efforts to strengthen the Japanese Yen. However, he warns Governor Ueda may sound cautious versus aggressive market pricing for 90bps of hikes.

item.title: Swiss National Bank: Inflation pressures build – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s European Economics team, led by Josie Anderson, George Buckley and Andrzej Szczepaniak, expects the Swiss National Bank to keep its policy rate at 0.00% at the September 2026 meeting.

item.title: US Initial Jobless Claims dropped to 196K last week
item.description: According to a report from the US Department of Labor (DOL) released on Thursday, the number of US citizens submitting new unemployment insurance applications decreased to 196K for the week ending September 12.

item.title: Bank of Japan: Market-priced hike to 1.25% – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team expects the Bank of Japan to raise its policy rate to 1.25%, a move they say is largely priced in as market expectations tightened in recent weeks.

item.title: British Pound weakens against Japanese Yen as BoE leaves rates unchanged
item.description: GBP/JPY trades under pressure on Thursday as the British Pound weakens across the board following the Bank of England’s (BoE) latest monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 208.23, down 0.40% on the day.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Hawkish path extends into year-end – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s FX Research team, including Charlie Lay and colleagues, highlight a hawkish shift from the Federal Reserve as it raised the Fed funds target range by 25bp to 3.75–4.00%. The updated dot plot points to another hike this year and higher rates through 2028.

item.title: Silver price rebounds on softer Oil but Fed tightening caps recovery
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) rebounds on Thursday and trades around $64.15 at the time of writing, up 1.87% on the day. The white metal benefits mainly from the pullback in Oil prices, which helps ease concerns about a renewed acceleration in inflationary pressures.

item.title: Euro jumps against British Pound as BoE leaves rates on hold
item.description: The Euro (EUR) rallies on Thursday as the British Pound (GBP) dives across the board as the Bank of England (BoE) left interest rates unchanged, with most of the other major central banks tightening their monetary policies.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: 20-day EMA acts as key barrier near 156.45
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) outperforms its major currency peers on Thursday, with the USD/JPY trading 0.28% lower to near 155.80.

item.title: US Dollar: Hawkish Fed supports Dollar near term – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong notes that the Fed’s 25bp hike and higher dots have extended the US Dollar (USD) rebound, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) around 100.3. Wong stresses that substantial Fed tightening is already priced, so softer US data could reopen USD downside.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Short-term downside toward 0.7050 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note AUD/USD dropped to 0.7075 and closed at 0.7087 after an overdone decline. For the next 24 hours, the pair is expected to stay within 0.7070–0.7115 with risks still skewed lower.

item.title: Massive selloff: Swiss Franc plunges 2% in five days amid growing SNB-Fed divergence
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) consolidates losses at 16-month lows against the US Dollar (USD) after dropping more than 2% in the previous five trading days.

item.title: Euro: Fair value falls on oil and Fed pressure against US Dollar - ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING highlights that EUR/USD has broken lower after a more hawkish‑than‑expected Federal Reserve meeting, with the two‑year swap differential at its widest since July.
